title: Sioux City Bandits brace for three-game home stretch with sights set on climbing NAL standings - NewsBreak
text:
By Anthony Mitchell No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
SIOUX CITY, Iowa (KCAU) – The Sioux City Bandits enter the halfway point of the season with a 3-2 record and look to continue its climb up the NAL standings, looking forward to the opportunities that are ahead with the team’s three-game homestand.
Sioux City closed out its four-game road trip with a three-point loss at undefeated and NAL leading-Southwest Kansas, but battled back to take down the Salina Liberty 47-46 in the team’s first home game on Saturday.
The Bandits hold a half game lead over Colorado for fourth place, but have a chance to move into the top three with a win on Saturday.
Sioux City has taken away plenty from a tumultous couple of weeks, emphasizing the importance of leaning on eachother and eliminating self-inflicted mistakes.
“At this point, what has hurt us in our two losses is very untimely mistakes. We miss a block on third and two and now we’re at fourth. Now we don’t convert a fourth down because we miss a block. We drop a pass in the wrong spot. We get a holding penalty. It’s been inopportune mistakes. So just eliminating those mistakes at crucial times and focusing a little bit more, that’s kind of what we’ve been harping on the guys about.” Bandits head coach Erv Strohbeen said.
Sioux City returns to action on Saturday at home against the Pueblo Punishers. Kickoff is set for 7:10 p.m.
